gen-dafont-existence-gf-scope-one: Existence has industrial, wide-porthole counters, and every part of a letter seems to carry the same visual mass. Scope One answers with stubby ascenders, a big x-height and counters that spill into the space around them.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-slabo-13px: Existence is built from uniform-width strokes, with round, glassy counters and terminals cut short of the bowl. Slabo 13px is bookish and dignified, its large open counters on a, e and s making a paragraph feel unhurried.
gen-dafont-franchise-fs-asap: Franchise packs lanky lowercase into a narrow ascender strip, its letters jammed shoulder to shoulder in one unbroken line weight. Asap has a body height close to its capitals, so a modest size for it and a much bigger one for the heading would feel right.
gen-dafont-franchise-fs-epilogue: Franchise crams its stretched lowercase together with a strong, clean look, while its c tips pull well apart from each other. Epilogue loosens everything with curvy, wire-like monoline sans-serif letters.
gen-dafont-franchise-fs-public-sans: Strong and clean, Franchise squeezes its elongated lowercase into tight rows with n arches as thick as the stems. And Public Sans does the opposite job, with a hefty lowercase and broad open counters on c and s.
gen-dafont-franchise-general-sans: Franchise stretches its lowercase up into a narrow ascender strip and jams the characters against each other. General Sans keeps a steady pen pressure and an x-height filling the line, so shrinking the heading would lose that punch.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-epunda-slab: Epunda Slab shows a visibly gaping c and rounded, lofty lowercase forms with a dignified, traditional air. Franchise sits against it as a strong, clean heading whose terminals end at the same width they began, all crowded together.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-fauna-one: Strong and clean, Franchise looks bent from wire. Fauna One follows in a literary serif, with shallow ascenders and descenders around a lofty middle band and a generous entry into the e's eye.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-glegoo: Refined and editorial, Glegoo has big counters and curved letters with wide, unclosed mouths. Franchise is the opposite, strong and clean, drawn with the line weight of a technical drawing pen.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-hanuman: Crowded, wiry and strong, Franchise holds its rounds and stems in one weight. And Hanuman has a high-waisted lowercase with wide-set terminals on s, so give it comfortable size beside the heading.
